findings: AssemblyCount presents a realistic, nontrivial business problem distinct from the named prior demo domains.
The rubric covers mandatory behavior, exclusions, contradictions, independent work, privacy, persistence and publication authorization while permitting alternative sound designs.
Critical semantic failures are distinguished from minor presentation issues; the director-policy contradiction does not block ordinary-motion work.
Supplied native boundary records include successful public access and denied private and rubric-alias reads. Freeze verification and the zero-row Planner query support pre-evaluation readiness.
No Planner architecture, graph, manual increments, execution permission or unsupported product-test claims are supplied.
review.rationale: The specification and structured interpretation are substantively aligned and source-traceable. Supplied verification records support the frozen evaluation and enforced isolation; verification of product behavior remains proposed work.
